summary: This plan rebuilt cpu-sec-test-env as a single repository that builds and runs the cpu-sec-bench security benchmark on every supported architecture: an x86_64 native reference lane, an aarch64 lane that executes the host-built corpus through the kernel's binfmt_misc handler under qemu-aarch64 with pointer-authentication, branch-target-identification and memory-tagging variants, a riscv64 system lane that boots a Linux 6.18.56 guest built from pinned sources under qemu-system-riscv64 with results extracted over a virtio-9p share, and a CHERI dialect probe against freshly built CHERI-LLVM and Morello-LLVM toolchains. The design keeps every pin in env.sh as the single source of truth, derives the bench registry at deploy time so per-lane expected failures are declared rather than hard-coded, and enforces one-lane-at-a-time access through an advisory lock on build/.lane.lock because the benchmark submodule is a single mutable workdir consumed read-only at a pinned commit. The riscv64 image is byte-reproducible: identity pins for the kernel build, normalized mtimes, LC_ALL=C ordering, and cpio --reproducible so inode numbers stay out of the newc headers, a defect the tester found and the plan fixed and re-verified across three independent clean deploys. The lane scripts live under scripts/common, scripts/aarch64, scripts/riscv64 and scripts/cheri, orchestrated by the Makefile lane dispatcher, with the derived registry and corpus builder shared in scripts/common. Trade-offs and gotchas: the riscv64 CPU model must be rva23s64 because the distro cross toolchain tags every executable RVA64-profile RVA23U64, the guest kernel must default-enable userspace vector, the CHERI lanes are deliberately probe-only with full bring-up deferred, and two CFI records are skipped on riscv64 because the bench's independent-assembly source still carries an untranslated x86 return site.
